==English==
{{wikidata lexeme|L4578}}

===Alternative forms===
* {{alt|en|distribucion||obsolete}}

===Etymology===
From {{uder|en|fro|distribution}}, from {{der|en|la|distributio}}, from {{m|la|distribuere||to distribute}}, itself from {{m|la|dis-||apart}} + {{m|la|tribuere||to assign, allot}} (from {{m|la|tribus}}). {{surf|en|distribute|-ion}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˌdɪstɹɪˈbjuːʃən/|a=RP}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˌdɪstɹɪˈbjuʃən/|/ˌdɪstɹəˈbjuʃən/|a=GA,CA}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-distribution.ogg|a=California|IPA=[ˌdɪs.tɹɪˈbjɪ.ʃən]}}
** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Naomi Persephone Amethyst (NaomiAmethyst)-distribution.wav|a=North Carolina}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˌdɪstɹɪˈbjʉːʃən/|a=AU}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˌdəstɹəˈbjʉːʃən/|a=NZ}}
* {{rhymes|en|uːʃən|s=4}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun|~}}

[[File:46v1 New-Sheet.jpg|thumb|Mind map]]

# An act of [[distribute|distributing]] or state of being distributed.
# An [[apportionment]] by [[law]] (of [[funds]], [[property]]).
# {{lb|en|business|marketing}} The [[process]] by which [[goods]] get to [[final]] [[consumer]]s over a geographical market, including [[storing]], [[selling]], [[shipping]] and [[advertising]].
# Anything distributed; [[portion]]; [[share]].
#* '''December 6, 1709''', {{w|Francis Atterbury}}, ''a sermon preach'd before the sons of the clergy at their anniversary-meeting in the Church of St. Paul''
# The [[result]] of distributing; [[arrangement]].
#* {{RQ:en:CNN|author=Hafsa Khalil|title=Electric blue tarantula species discovered in Thailand|url=https://www.cnn.com/2023/09/26/world/electric-blue-tarantula-discovered-thailand-scn-scli-intl|date=2023-09-26|passage=A group of Thai researchers found the spider during an expedition to Phang-Nga province in southern Thailand to research the diversity and '''distribution''' of tarantulas in the country.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20241120202900/https://www.cnn.com/2023/09/26/world/electric-blue-tarantula-discovered-thailand-scn-scli-intl/}}
#* {{quote-book|en|passage=To specify the effect of flutter with one figure can be extremely misleading, for it says nothing about the '''distribution''' of flutter in the spectrum of interest.|page=200|url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/Data_in_Medicine_Collection_Processing_a/JWMyBwAAQBAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=%22flutter+in+the%22+magnetic+recording&pg=PA200&printsec=frontcover|publisher=Springer Netherlands|title=Data in Medicine: Collection, Processing and Presentation: A Physical-Technical Introduction for Physicians and Biologists|editor=J. Strackee, Robert S. Reneman|year=1979}}
# The total number of something sold or delivered to the clients.
#: {{ux|en|The '''distribution''' of my little rock magazine is about 3,000.}}
# The [[frequency]] of [[occurrence]] or [[extent]] of [[existence]].
# {{lb|en|economics}} The apportionment of income or wealth in a population.
#: {{ux|en|The wealth '''distribution''' became extremely skewed in the kleptocracy.}}
# {{lb|en|card games}} The way in which a player's [[hand]] is divided in [[suit|suits]], or in which a particular suit is divided between the players.
#: {{ux|en|The declarer had 3-6-2-2 '''distribution'''.}}
# {{lb|en|mathematics|statistics}} A [[probability distribution]]; the set of [[relative]] likelihoods that a variable will have a value in a given interval. {{C|en|Functions}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|author=Elie Mystal|title=NALP Gives More Information on Expected Lawyer Salary|magazine={{w|Above the Law (website)|Above the Law}}|url=https://abovethelaw.com/2010/07/nalp-gives-more-information-on-expected-lawyer-salary/|date=2010-07-23|passage=In fact, NALP has been at the forefront of educating prospective lawyers on the dangers of focusing on “average” starting salaries. The average is meaningless. The median is just slightly more helpful, and NALP has been begging people to pay attention to the bimodal salary '''distribution''' curve that tells the true story of how much lawyers are likely to get paid.|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/Rk6Gq|archivedate=2023-10-15}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=2015-09-11|author=|title=Hotspots of Malaria Transmission in the Peruvian Amazon: Rapid Assessment through a Parasitological and Serological Survey|journal=PLOS ONE|url=http://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0137458|doi=10.1371/journal.pone.0137458|volume=|issue=|pages=
|passage=The criterion for positivity was determined for each antigen of each species applying a mixture model to the PP data which assumed two inherent Gaussian '''distributions''': a narrow '''distribution''' or seronegatives, and a broader '''distribution''' of seropositives.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20240312134617/https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0137458}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=2015-12-11|author=|title=On the Role of Histamine Receptors in the Regulation of Circadian Rhythms|journal=PLOS ONE|url=http://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0144694|doi=10.1371/journal.pone.0144694|volume=|issue=|pages=
|passage=Similarly, the brain-penetrating ''Hrh2'' antagonist zolantidine had no effect on light-induced phase shift as shown for hamsters, or the lengths or '''distributions''' of NREM, REM and wakefulness states as shown on rats. |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20250121102440/https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0144694}}
# {{lb|en|mathematics|differential geometry}} A [[subset]] of the [[tangent bundle]] of a [[manifold]] that satisfies certain properties; ''used to construct the notions of [[integrability]] and [[foliation]] of a manifold''.
# {{senseid|en|software bundle}} {{lb|en|software}} A set of [[bundle]]d [[software]] [[component]]s.
#: {{syn|en|distro}}
#: {{ux|en|a Linux '''distribution'''}}
# {{lb|en|finance}} The process or result of the sale of securities, especially their placement among investors with long-term investment strategies.
# {{lb|en|logic}} The [[resolution]] of a [[whole]] into its [[part]]s.
# {{lb|en|printing|historical}} The process of [[sort]]ing the [[type]]s and placing them in their proper [[box]]es in the [[case]]s.
# {{lb|en|steam engines}} The steps or operations by which [[steam]] is supplied to and withdrawn from the [[cylinder]] at each [[stroke]] of the [[piston]]: admission, suppression or cutting off, release or exhaust, and compression of exhaust steam prior to the next admission.
# {{lb|en|rhetoric}} A rhetorical technique in which a subject is divided into multiple cases based on some property or properties, and each case is addressed individually.
#* '''1728''', {{w|Ephraim Chambers}}, ''[[w:Cyclopædia, or an Universal Dictionary of Arts and Sciences|Cyclopædia]]'' I, [https://archive.org/stream/Cyclopediachambers-Volume1/cyclo1#page/n595/mode/2up page 230/2] ''s.v.'' “'''Diſtribution'''²”:

===Etymology 1===
From {{der|en|enm|schete}}; partly from {{der|en|ang|sċīete||a sheet, a piece of linen cloth}}; partly from {{der|en|ang|sċēata||a corner, angle; the lower corner of a sail, sheet}}; and {{der|en|ang|sċēat||a corner, angle}}; all from {{der|en|gem-pro|*skautijǭ}}, {{m|gem-pro|*skautaz||corner, wedge, lap}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*(s)kewd-||to throw, shoot, pursue, rush}}.

Cognate with {{cog|frr|skut||the fold of a garment, lap, coattail}}, {{cog|fy|skoat||sheet; sail; lap}}, {{cog|nl|schoot||the fold of a garment, lap, sheet}}, {{cog|nds-de|Schote||a line from the foot of a sail}}, {{cog|de|Schoß||the fold of a garment, lap}}, {{cog|da|skød||lap, skirt}}, {{cog|is|skaut||the corner of a cloth, a line from the foot of a sail, the skirt or sleeve of a garment, a hood}}, {{cog|no|skaut||headdress}}, {{cog|sv|sköt||sheet}}.

====Noun====
{{en-noun}}

# {{cap|bedsheet}}; a thin bed [[cloth]] used as a [[covering]] for a [[mattress]] or as a layer over the sleeper.
#: {{ux|en|Use the '''sheets''' in the hall closet to make the bed.}}
#* {{RQ:KJV|Acts|10|10-11|text=He fell into a trance, and saw heaven opened, and a certain vessel descending unto him, as it had been a great '''sheet''' knit at the four corners.}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Othello|IV|iii|passage=If I do die before thee, prithee, shroud me / In one of those same '''sheets'''.}}
# A piece of [[paper]], usually rectangular, that has been prepared for writing, artwork, drafting, wrapping, manufacture of packaging (boxes, envelopes, etc.), and for other uses. The word does not include scraps and irregular small pieces destined to be recycled, used for stuffing or cushioning or [[papier-mâché]], etc. In modern books, each sheet of paper is typically folded in half, to produce two [[leaf|leaves]] and four [[page]]s. In the absence of folding, "leaf" and "sheet" are equivalent.
#: {{holonyms|en|signature|quire}}
#: {{meronyms|en|leaf|folium|page}}
#: {{ux|en|A '''sheet''' of paper measuring eight and one-half inches wide by eleven inches high is a popular item in commerce.}}
#: {{ux|en|Paper is designated “20 pound” if a stack (ream) of 500 '''sheets''' 22 inches by 17 inches weighs 20 pounds.}}
## {{lb|en|figurative}} {{q|originally referring to a printed [[document]]}} A [[summary]] or [[record]] of key information, especially an [[official]] one; the information contained in such a document.
##: {{co|en|rap '''sheet''', style '''sheet''', material safety data'''sheet''', balance '''sheet'''}}
# A [[flat]] metal [[pan]], often without raised edge, used for [[bake|baking]].
#: {{ux|en|Place the rolls on the cookie '''sheet''', edges touching, and bake for 10-11 minutes.}}
# A [[thin]], flat piece or [[layer]] of solid material.
#: {{ux|en|The [[glazer]] cut several [[panes]] from a large '''sheet''' of glass.}}
#: {{ux|en|A '''sheet''' of that new silicon stuff is as good as a '''sheet''' of tinfoil to keep food from sticking in the baking pan.}}
# A [[broad]], flat expanse or covering of a material on a [[surface]].
#: {{ux|en|Mud froze on the road in a solid '''sheet''', then more rain froze into a '''sheet''' of ice on top of the mud!}}
# {{lb|en|figuratively|}} {{q|Usually used in the plural}} An [[expanse]] or intense [[wave]] of something [[fluid]] (such as [[fire]] or [[precipitation]]), conceptualized as hanging, suspended, falling, or moving in a particular direction.{{attn|en|improve?}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1908|title=Pillar of Fire|page=15
|text=... '''sheets''' of fire could be seen. The air became intensely hot and they knew that the forest-fire was upon them.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1988|title=A Twin-mirrored Galvanometer Laser Light Sheet Generator
|text=... '''sheets''' of light which appear to be formed by a source at one location for horizontal sheets and another location for vertical sheets. This is the direct result of the relative displacement of the two scanners along the optical axis{{nb...}}}}
# {{lb|en|nautical}} A [[line]] (rope) used to adjust the [[trim]] of a [[sail]].
#: {{ux|en|To be "three sheets to the wind" is to say that a four-cornered sail is tethered only by one '''sheet''' and thus the sail is useless.}}
# {{lb|en|nautical|nonstandard}} A [[sail]].
#* {{RQ:Dryden Annus Mirabilis|passage=Their folded '''Sheets''' dismiss the useless Air}}
# {{lb|en|curling}} The area of [[ice]] on which the game of [[curling]] is played.
# {{lb|en|nonstandard}} A layer of [[veneer]].
# {{lb|en|geology}} An extensive [[bed]] of an eruptive [[rock]] intruded between, or overlying, other [[stratum|strata]].
# {{lb|en|nautical}} The space in the [[forward]] or [[after]] part of a [[boat]] where there are no [[rower]]s.
#: {{ux|en|fore '''sheets'''; stern '''sheets'''}}
# {{lb|en|video games|dated}} A distinct [[level]] or [[stage]] within a game.
#*: The gecko moves from left to right and you must catch him when he calls. {{...}} On the second '''sheet''' you must stand under the Gecko in the tree and jump, and on the third '''sheet''' you must catch the Gecko's friend.
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=1984|month=February|journal=Sinclair Programs
|passage=If you land safely you will gain 30 extra points and move to the next '''sheet'''.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=1984|author=Chris Passey; Matthew Uffindell|title=Run It Again|journal=Crash|issue=4|url=http://www.crashonline.org.uk/04/runit.htm
|passage=What distinguishes ''Eskimo Eddie'' from the others is that it has two totally different '''sheets''' in the game. {{...}} In the first '''sheet''', Frogger style, you have to rescue Percy penguin from Growler the bear.}}

===Etymology===
From {{inh|en|enm|gud mornynge}} (also as {{m|enm|goode morne}}, {{m|enm|gode morne}}), from {{inh|en|ang|*gōdne morgen|t=good morning}}, an ellipsis for an expression such as "I wish you a good morning", equivalent to {{af|en|good|morning}}. Compare {{cog|fy|goeie moarn}}, {{cog|nl|goedemorgen}}, {{cog|de|guten Morgen}}, {{cog|da|god morgen}}, {{cog|sv|god morgon}}, {{cog|is|góðan morgunn}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˌɡʊd ˈmɔːnɪŋ/|a=RP}}
** {{audio|en|En-uk-good morning.ogg}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˌɡʊd ˈmɔɹnɪŋ/|a=US}}
** {{audio|en|En-us-good morning.ogg}}

===Interjection===
{{en-intj}}

# {{non-gloss|Used as a [[greeting]] when meeting someone for the first time in the [[morning]].}}
#: {{syn|en|good morrow<ll:archaic>}}
#: {{ux|en|The teacher welcomed the kids to school with "'''Good morning''', boys and girls."}}
# {{lb|en|less common|more formal}} {{non-gloss|A [[parting]] in the morning.}}
#: {{ux|en|Thank you for coming everyone and I hope to see you again next year. '''Good morning'''.}}
#* {{RQ:Tolkien Hobbit|edition=revised|page=19|passage=“'''Good morning'''!” he said at last. “We don’t want any adventures here, thank you!{{nb...}}” By this he meant that the conversation was at an end. / “What a lot of things you do use '''''Good morning''''' for!” said Gandalf. “Now you mean that you want to get rid of me,{{nb...}}”}}
# {{lb|en|by extension|humorous}} {{non-gloss|Used to greet someone who has just [[awaken]]ed (irrespective of the time of day).}}
#: {{ux|en|Up at the crack of dusk! '''Good morning'''!}}
# {{lb|en|by extension|informal}} {{non-gloss|Said to someone who has come to a [[belated]] [[realization]].}}
#: {{ux|en|You're just realizing that now? '''Good morning'''!}}

====Usage notes====
* May be shortened in casual speech to {{l|en|morning}}.
* As a greeting, may be used by anyone in almost any setting from the most casual to the most formal, close friend or stranger, regardless of age, social group, etc.

{{phrasebook|en|Greetings}}

===Alternative forms===
* {{alter|en|good-evening||dated}}

===Etymology===
An ellipsis for an expression such as "I wish you a good evening.".

===Pronunciation===
* {{audio|en|en-us-good_evening.ogg|a=US}}
* {{audio|en|En-uk-good_evening.ogg|a=UK}}

===Interjection===
{{en-intj}}

# {{lb|en|generally formal in|_|US|Canada}} {{non-gloss|Used as a [[greeting]] in the [[evening]]}}.
#: {{syn|en|good-den<q:[[Appendix:Glossary#obsolete|obsolete]]>}}
#: {{ux|en|'''Good evening''' everyone and welcome to our 34th annual general meeting.}}

====Usage notes====
{{lb|en|US|Canada}} ''Good evening'' is generally considered quite formal, such as by a television news anchor or at the beginning of an address to an audience. An exception is if it is said with exaggeration and with a smile, such as in "''Good evening'' ladies! You are all looking lovely as usual."
